headline: Drupal's KEV-listed RCE leads a day of active exploitation and high-value breaches
standfirst: A critical Drupal Core remote-code-execution flaw is now KEV-listed and actively exploited, while two GeoServer flaws are also under attack and a critical NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free demands triage. Elsewhere, a reported CIA breach, a confirmed FinCEN intrusion, a Check Point management-server campaign, suspected hospital ransomware and Australia's new duty-of-care law round out the day.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

The lead item is Drupal Core's Fail2Install flaw, CVE-2026-132165, a CVSS 9.8 remote code execution issue that CISA has added to KEV [[s24]]. The catalog entry confirms known exploitation and directs federal agencies to apply mitigations under BOD 26-04; that requirement is agency-specific, not a universal deadline. Ransomware campaign use is listed as unknown. Exploit details are reported to be emerging, but the supplied excerpt does not describe the exploit chain or affected Drupal versions.

GeoServer is the second active-exploitation item: CVE-2026-120705, an arbitrary file read rated 8.6, and CVE-2026-129243 are being exploited, with researchers warning they can chain to unauthenticated RCE [[s21]]. The second flaw's severity is not supplied. Neither appears in KEV in the supplied fields—a catalog miss, not proof that exploitation has not occurred.

## Breaches

Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the CIA [[s38]]. Details of access, data and attribution were not supplied. Analysis: if confirmed, an intrusion into an intelligence-analysis platform raises counterintelligence and source-exposure concerns beyond a routine breach, but the excerpt supports only the reported compromise.

FinCEN said unauthorized access hit a limited subset of its systems and took some systems offline as a precaution [[s22]]. The bureau collects suspicious activity reports and other BSA filings. Analysis: offline systems at a financial-intelligence bureau raise reporting-disruption questions, though the excerpt does not confirm deadline changes or data loss.

Twenty-four Check Point Security Management servers were compromised across 22 organizations worldwide by an unknown threat actor using suspected AI-driven offensive tooling, tracked as GT13 [[s39]]. Listed sectors include financial services, energy and government. Analysis: management servers are high-value because they can govern security controls, but the excerpt does not specify access, persistence or data taken.

A suspected ransomware attack impaired the University Hospital of Guadeloupe's systems, forcing postponed surgeries, suspension of some cancer treatments and a return to pen and paper; the national cybersecurity agency is investigating [[s20]]. The attack is suspected, not confirmed, and the operational impact is the story.

## Vulnerabilities

The NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free CVE-2026-123633 is rated CVSS 4.0 9.2 Critical and CWE-416 [[s42]]. NVD says exploitation requires HTTP/2 client connections and proxying to a backend, with a crafted request triggering use-after-free when the worker is low on worker_connections. Impact is denial of service, or code execution if ASLR is disabled or bypassed; there is no control-plane exposure. Affected configurations include NGINX Open Source, NGINX Plus, Ingress Controller, Gateway Fabric, Instance Manager and WAF. No KEV listing is supplied. Analysis: high attack complexity and configuration dependence mean the headline CVSS score alone is a poor exposure test.

## Industry

Australia's Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, requiring online providers to establish protocols protecting users from threats of violence and rape and from behavior that could cause significant harms [[s7]]. The mandate is framed around preempting foreseeable harms. Analysis: it could become a regulatory template beyond Australia, but the excerpt does not detail enforcement, penalties or covered services.

selected.title: NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633
selected.excerpt: Technical analysis of CVE-2026-123633, an NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free flaw, with details on affected versions, sanitizer tests, and patch guidance. The post NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633 appeared first on Unit 42.

nvd.description:
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

selected.angle: Critical NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free (CVE-2026-123633, CVSS 9.2) affects widely deployed web infrastructure and needs patch triage.
